ruleTitle: Do you use pure black for text or backgrounds?
reason: Pure black (#000000) is used on 14 text elements. A soft dark tone like #222 reads easier.

checkpoint.requiredActions:
Avoid using pure black (#000000) for text or backgrounds. Opt for softer dark tones like charcoal (#333333) for text and off-black colors for backgrounds.

Use high contrast between text and background, but ensure the tone isn't too harsh on the eyes, improving readability and visual comfort.

**Detailed Actions:**
- **Text:** Use colors with slightly lighter shades (e.g., #333333 or #444444) for body text instead of pure black. These tones reduce the starkness that pure black creates, making reading less fatiguing, especially for longer sessions.
- **Backgrounds:** Avoid using pure black (#000000) as a background color. Instead, choose a dark gray like #212121 or #121212. This ensures that text and images stand out while reducing visual strain.
- **Contrast:** Ensure there’s sufficient contrast between text and background, especially for accessibility. Use tools like  [Contrast Checker](https://webaim.org/resources/contrastchecker/) to verify that your combinations meet accessibility standards.
checkpoint.justificationsBenefits:
Pure black creates too much contrast, causing eye strain over time. Softer colors improve the reading experience and make the website feel more professional and easier to engage with.

This small tweak can significantly improve user experience by enhancing readability and comfort, keeping users on your site longer and increasing the likelihood of conversions.

**Additional Resources:**
- [Color Contrast And Why You Should Rethink It](https://www.smashingmagazine.com/2014/10/color-contrast-tips-and-tools-for-accessibility/)
- [Contrast Checker](https://webaim.org/resources/contrastchecker/)

ruleTitle: Do button and link labels start with a verb and convey urgency (e.g., "Shop Now")?
reason: The main call to action button is labeled 'ADD TO CART', which is an action verb but does not convey urgency.

checkpoint.requiredActions:
Make sure all button and link labels start with action verbs and convey a sense of urgency. Labels like “Shop Now” or “Get Yours Today” are clear and actionable, guiding users toward making a purchase.

**Detailed Actions:**
- **Start with a Strong Verb:** Every button label should start with a verb that describes the action users will take, such as "Buy," "Explore," or "Save." Use language that directly signals what will happen when the button is clicked.
- **Convey Urgency:** Add a sense of immediacy by using words like “Now,” “Today,” or “Limited Time” where relevant. This creates a subtle pressure, nudging users to act promptly.
- **Customize Language for Context:** Ensure buttons align with the specific goal of the page. For example, on a product page, "Add to Cart" or "Buy Now" works well, while on a homepage, “Explore Collection” might fit better.

**WooCommerce and Shopify Tips:**
- For WooCommerce, go to **Appearance > Customize** and adjust button text in your theme settings if available. Some themes support custom labels for product and checkout pages without additional plugins.
- On Shopify, use the **Theme Editor** under **Online Store > Themes > Customize** to modify button labels. Most Shopify themes allow easy button text customization on product and homepage sections directly from the editor.
checkpoint.justificationsBenefits:
Action-focused, urgent labels guide users directly toward completing key actions, reducing hesitation and helping users understand the purpose of each button. Urgency motivates quicker action, which can significantly improve conversion rates.

**Additional Resources:**
- [Baymard Institute’s guidelines on Button UX](https://baymard.com/learn/button-design) – Details on effective button labeling.
- [Smashing Magazine: Call to Action Button Best Practices](https://www.smashingmagazine.com/2009/10/call-to-action-buttons-examples-and-best-practices/) – Insights into how action-oriented language impacts user behavior.

ruleTitle: Is the most common size/color preselected?
reason: No size or color is preselected; the shopper must choose a size before adding to cart.

checkpoint.requiredActions:
Preselect the most common size/color to streamline the purchasing process.

We suggest test this point against **"Is there a reminder to select size/color if users forget before adding to the cart?"**

**Pros**: Can streamline the purchasing process, reducing friction for users who prefer default choices, and speeding up the path to checkout.

**Cons**: Increases the risk of users accidentally adding the wrong size/variant, potentially increasing returns and customer dissatisfaction, especially in categories like clothing where fit is crucial.

Balancing ease of use with ensuring informed decisions is key. Testing will help identify the optimal approach, allowing for data-driven decisions tailored to the specific product category.
checkpoint.justificationsBenefits: Streamlines the purchasing process, reducing friction for users who prefer default choices, and speeding up the path to checkout.

ruleTitle: Is lazy loading enabled for images and videos?
reason: 23 of 25 images load only when needed (lazy loading).

checkpoint.requiredActions:
Ensure that lazy loading is enabled for all images and videos on your site to improve load time and user experience.

**Detailed Actions**:
- Lazy loading means images and videos only load when they come into view, which reduces initial page load time. If your theme doesn't support it by default, implementing a plugin or editing your theme’s code may be necessary.

**For WooCommerce and Shopify Users:**
- **Shopify**
    - Most modern Shopify themes have lazy loading built-in. Check your theme settings or install an app like **[Tiny SEO Speed Image Optimizer](https://apps.shopify.com/smart-image-optimizer)** to enable it for non-video content.
- **WooCommerce**
    - If your theme doesn't support lazy loading, you can enable it through settings or use a plugin like **[WP Rocket](https://wp-rocket.me/)** or **[Smush](https://wordpress.org/plugins/wp-smushit/)** that adds lazy loading functionality.

⚠️ Please avoid lazy loading images above the fold. They need to load first and fast.
checkpoint.justificationsBenefits:
Lazy loading reduces initial page load time and bandwidth usage by loading media only when it comes into view. Fast-loading pages are crucial for higher conversions, as users are less likely to abandon slow sites.

**Additional Resources:**
- [Browser-level image lazy loading for the web](https://web.dev/articles/browser-level-image-lazy-loading)
- [Improving your online store performance](https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/online-store/web-performance/improving-web-performance)

ruleTitle: Are product titles and descriptions concise, informative, and consistent?
reason: The product title 'Women's Wool Cruiser Slip On' is concise and informative. The description highlights key benefits and materials.

checkpoint.requiredActions:
Make sure your product titles are clear, concise, and descriptive, focusing on key attributes (e.g., brand, model, color, size). Descriptions should briefly outline product benefits and specifications.

**Detailed Actions:**
- **Product Titles**
    - Keep titles under 50 characters.
    - Include essential details like the product type, brand, and key features (e.g., “Nike Air Zoom Sneakers”).
    - Avoid unnecessary keywords or jargon that clutter the title.
- **Consistency**
    - Ensure that all product titles follow a similar format across your category pages for a uniform experience.
    - Avoid using different terminology for the same products or product types (e.g., don’t alternate between “T-shirt” and “Tee” in titles or descriptions).
checkpoint.justificationsBenefits:
Clear, concise, and consistent product titles and descriptions enhance the shopping experience by making it easy for customers to find the products they want and understand their value quickly. It reduces cognitive load, leading to higher conversion rates.

**Additional Resources:**
- [How To Write a Product Description (Examples + Template)](https://www.shopify.com/blog/8211159-9-simple-ways-to-write-product-descriptions-that-sell)
- [14 Best Tactics To Optimize Ecommerce Product Titles for Conversions](https://textcortex.com/post/product-title-optimization-best-ecommerce-tactics)

ruleTitle: Is the product’s material or composition information clearly provided?

checkpoint.requiredActions:

- Use bullet points for clarity and consistency, making sure the details are easy to read.
- If the product comes in multiple variations (e.g., different fabrics or materials), make sure the content is updated accordingly or display a dropdown or selectable option so users can see the material composition for each variant.

ruleTitle: Is the free shipping threshold (if applicable) highlighted near the main CTA?
reason: The free shipping threshold is displayed directly below the add to cart button.

checkpoint.requiredActions:
Make the free shipping threshold visible near the "Add to Cart" or "Buy Now" button to encourage customers to increase their order size. Display it in a clear, prominent, and visually appealing way.

**Detailed Actions:**
- **Placement**: Ensure the free shipping threshold message is placed near key CTAs like "Add to Cart," "Buy Now," or "Proceed to Checkout." The closer to the decision-making process, the better.
- **Messaging**: Use clear, direct language such as "Add $X more to get free shipping!" or "You’re just $X away from free shipping!"
- **Visuals**: Make the message stand out with a contrasting color or design that draws attention but doesn’t overpower the CTA.
- **Consistency**: If the site offers free shipping based on different conditions (e.g., specific product categories), make sure the messaging is dynamic and adapts based on the customer’s cart.
- **User-Friendly**: Ensure the message is mobile-responsive and easy to spot on all devices, especially mobile, where users are less likely to notice subtle design elements.
checkpoint.justificationsBenefits: Highlighting free shipping thresholds encourages customers to add more items to their cart to qualify, increasing average order value (AOV).

ruleTitle: Are dropdown menus easy to use on both desktop and mobile?
reason: The page does not use dropdown menus for navigation or product options.

checkpoint.requiredActions:
Implement touch-friendly dropdowns with clear labels and avoid multiple levels that can be difficult to navigate on touch screens.

**Detailed Actions:**
- **Design for Touch:** For mobile, ensure that dropdown menus are appropriately sized for touch interaction. The touch targets should be at least 44x44 pixels to accommodate finger taps comfortably.
- **Limit Menu Items:** Keep the number of items in dropdown menus manageable (ideally between 5-10 items) to prevent overwhelming users. Use submenus sparingly and ensure they are easy to access.
- **Visual Feedback:** Implement hover states on desktop and tap states on mobile to provide visual feedback when users interact with the dropdowns.
checkpoint.justificationsBenefits: Easy-to-use dropdown menus significantly enhance user experience by facilitating quick access to products and categories, which can lead to higher conversion rates. If users find navigation frustrating, they are more likely to abandon their shopping journey.

ruleTitle: Is the logo clickable and linked to the homepage?
reason: The Allbirds logo in the header is clickable and links to the homepage.

checkpoint.requiredActions:
Ensure the logo in the header is clickable and links back to the homepage, providing users with an easy way to start over.

**For WooCommerce and Shopify Users:**
- **Shopify**
    - Go to **Online Store > Themes**, then click on **Customize**. In the header section, ensure the logo is set to link back to the homepage.
- **WooCommerce**
    - Navigate to **Appearance > Customize > Site Identity**. Ensure that your logo is uploaded and linked correctly.
checkpoint.justificationsBenefits: Having a clickable logo linked to the homepage is a standard practice that enhances user navigation and reinforces branding. It allows users to easily return to the starting point, improving overall site usability and encouraging longer browsing sessions.

ruleTitle: Have you tested "color swatches" vs. "small images" of variants for the best user experience, especially in fashion?
reason: The page uses color swatches for color selection and numerical buttons for size selection.

checkpoint.requiredActions:
Do you know what works best for you? If you can do it, test the use of "color swatches" and "small images" for product variants to determine which provides the most intuitive, engaging, and conversion-boosting experience, especially for fashion products.

**Detailed Actions:**
- **Evaluate Product Variants:** Display product variants (e.g., color, size, material) using both "color swatches" and "small images" to understand which format your users prefer.
- **Run A/B Testing:** Implement A/B tests to track user engagement and conversion metrics for each variant display style. For fashion, color swatches tend to perform well for quick color selection, while small images might be preferred for products where the visual details (e.g., patterns, textures) are important.

**For WooCommerce and Shopify Users:**
- **Shopify**
    - Use Shopify’s built-in variant options
- **WooCommerce**
    - Use [Variation Swatches for WooCommerce](https://wordpress.org/plugins/woo-variation-swatches/)
checkpoint.justificationsBenefits: Different styles of variant selectors can impact user preference and engagement. Testing helps identify which approach improves the shopping experience and conversion rates.

ruleTitle: If the product includes additional items as a pack, are all included products visually displayed?
reason: The product is a single item and does not include additional items as a pack.

checkpoint.requiredActions:
Clearly list all included items near the CTA. Frame it as an extra value.

**Detailed Actions:**
- Add a “What’s Included” section directly below or next to the Add to Cart button.
- Ensure the list is concise yet complete, using bullet points or icons for clarity.

**Example Phrasing:**

- ✅ "**Get more for your money** – All accessories included, at no extra cost!"

ruleTitle: Is the main product title visually prominent?

checkpoint.requiredActions:
Make sure main product title is clearly visible, prominent, and easily readable. It should be the first thing users see when they land on the product page.

**Detailed Actions**:
- Use a large, bold font size that stands out from other page elements.
- Position the title at the top of the product section, ideally just above the product image or close to the "Add to Cart" button.
- Ensure the color of the text contrasts well with the background, making it easy to read on all devices.
- Avoid clutter around the title—ensure there is enough white space to make it stand out.
- Test different font styles and sizes to find the most effective presentation.

ruleTitle: Does the product page have clickable tabs for easy access to more product details?
reason: The product page does not have clickable tabs or accordions for additional product details.

checkpoint.requiredActions:
Implement clickable tabs (e.g., “Description,” “Reviews,” “Specifications”) for easy navigation to detailed information.

**Detailed Actions:**
- Implement tabs or accordion-style dropdowns that allow customers to quickly jump between sections of the product page without long scrolling.
- Keep the tab labels clear and concise (e.g., "Description," "Details," "Reviews," "Shipping").
- Ensure tabs are easy to interact with and responsive, especially on mobile devices. Make sure the active tab is highlighted for clarity.

checkpoint.justificationsBenefits:
Tabs help reduce page clutter, making it easier for users to find the information they need without excessive scrolling. This improves user experience, increases engagement, and reduces bounce rates.

ruleTitle: Are product images shown from multiple angles and perspectives to give a complete view?
reason: The product images show the shoes from multiple angles, including top, side, and bottom views.

checkpoint.requiredActions:
Ensure product images are displayed from various angles and perspectives, such as front, side, back, and close-up views, to provide a complete picture. Additionally, include context to demonstrate scale, such as showing the product alongside a reference object, to help customers visualize its actual size.

Use zoom or 360-degree functionality if possible and necessary, for furniture products particularly.

**Detailed Actions:**
- Upload high-quality images of the product from different angles and ensure they are clearly visible in the product gallery.
- Include close-ups of important product details (e.g., stitching, texture, or special features).
- Include images where the product is placed next to common items (e.g., a coffee cup, a coin, or a hand) to provide a reference for scale.
- If the product is wearable or has variable dimensions, add a model or mannequin wearing or holding the product to highlight its fit or size.
- For digital products (e.g., software or online services), use screenshots that show the product in use with a clear indication of its size in relation to other elements on the screen.
checkpoint.justificationsBenefits: Giving users a full view of the product builds trust and confidence in their purchase, especially for visually-driven products like apparel or furniture. Displaying scale and dimensions in product images helps eliminate confusion about size, making it easier for customers to gauge whether the product meets their expectations.

ruleTitle: Do product images include lifestyle shots that show the product in use?
reason: The page includes lifestyle shots showing the shoes being worn by a model in a natural setting.

checkpoint.requiredActions:
Incorporate lifestyle images that showcase the product being used in real-world scenarios to help users visualize its benefits.

Detailed Actions:
- Include at least 1-2 lifestyle images on each product page. These should complement product photos, showing the item in use in realistic settings.
- Focus on images where the product is being worn, used, or displayed in context. For example, if selling clothing, show people wearing it; if selling kitchen tools, show them in use in a kitchen environment.
- Choose settings and models that reflect your target audience. Make sure the shots are professionally taken to avoid pixelation or low-quality visuals.
- Use images that enhance the emotional appeal of the product and convey how it solves the customer’s problem or enhances their life.
checkpoint.justificationsBenefits: Lifestyle shots create a stronger emotional connection, helping customers visualize how the product fits into their lives. It enhances user experience, builds trust, and leads to higher conversion rates as shoppers can better imagine themselves using the product.

ruleTitle: Is there a section explaining how to use the product in simple steps?
reason: The product is shoes, which do not require a 'how to use' section.

checkpoint.requiredActions:
Include a clear, concise section on the product page that outlines how to use the product in simple, easy-to-understand steps. This could be a step-by-step guide, instructional video, or visual tutorial.

**Detailed Actions**
- Create a dedicated "How to Use" section on the product page that explains the product's usage in 3-5 simple steps.
- Use clear language and break down the process in bite-sized pieces, ideally with visuals (e.g., icons, images, or videos) accompanying each step.
- Include common scenarios or FAQs that potential buyers may have about the product's usage.
- For complex products, consider adding a "How-to" video demonstrating the product in action.
- Integrate these explanations close to the product description or in a tab section for easy accessibility.
checkpoint.justificationsBenefits: Including a clear "how to use" section reduces confusion and increases customer confidence, directly impacting conversions.

ruleTitle: Are relevant cross-sell or up-sell products displayed on the product page?
reason: There are no cross-sell or up-sell products displayed on the product page.

checkpoint.requiredActions:
Make sure relevant cross-sell (related items) or up-sell (higher-value items) products are prominently displayed on the product page to encourage additional purchases.

**Detailed Actions:**
- **Positioning:** Display cross-sell and up-sell products below or next to the main product description or image.
- **Relevance:** Use product data (e.g., related categories, purchase history, or customer behavior) to recommend items most likely to be bought together.
- **Design:** Keep the design clean and visually distinct, making sure the recommendations are easy to browse but not distracting from the primary product.

**For WooCommerce and Shopify Users:**
- **Shopify**
    - Use product recommendations that are powered by Shopify’s native algorithm, or apps like [Bold Upsell](https://apps.shopify.com/product-upsell?locale=fr) or [Frequently Bought Together](https://apps.shopify.com/frequently-bought-together) for advanced features.
- **WooCommerce**
    - Use the built-in "Related Products" feature. To enhance cross-sells or up-sells, consider plugins like [WooCommerce Product Recommendations](https://woocommerce.com/products/product-recommendations/).
checkpoint.justificationsBenefits:
Cross-sells and up-sells significantly boost average order value (AOV) by showing customers complementary or higher-value options they may be interested in, improving their shopping experience and increasing your revenue.

**Additional Resources:**
- [Upselling vs. Cross-Selling: The Ultimate Guide](https://www.shopify.com/blog/upselling-and-cross-selling)
- [How to use upsells and cross-sells on your Shopify product pages](https://instant.so/blog/how-to-use-upsells-and-cross-sells-on-your-shopify-product-pages)

ruleTitle: Do all product images have consistent backgrounds to maintain a professional appearance?
reason: The product images have consistent light-colored backgrounds for the product-only shots.

checkpoint.requiredActions:
Standardize image backgrounds across the product catalog. A clean, neutral background (e.g., white or light gray) helps maintain a professional, polished look across your product listings

**Detailed Actions:**
- Choose one background color or style for all product images and apply it to each product photo.
- Use image editing tools to remove any distractions and create a consistent look.
- Ensure that product photos are well-lit, clear, and focused, with no clutter or background elements competing for attention.
- If your product images are shot in different settings (e.g., some with white backgrounds, others in a lifestyle setting), consider removing the lifestyle images or editing them to match the consistent background theme.

Use this tool for free: <https://www.remove.bg/>
checkpoint.justificationsBenefits: Consistency in product imagery builds trust and improves the perceived professionalism of your site. A cluttered or inconsistent visual presentation can distract or confuse customers, negatively affecting their shopping experience.

Display images showing the product with complementary or related items, such as accessories, to encourage cross-selling and increase average order value.

- Use lifestyle images that show the product in use with complementary items in the frame, enhancing the customer's vision of how they can use the product in real life.
- Create a dedicated section or carousel in your product image gallery to highlight complementary items.

ruleTitle: Do you offer a quick complementary add-on upsell near the main CTA?
reason: There is no quick complementary add-on upsell presented near the 'Add to Cart' button.

checkpoint.requiredActions:
Identify complementary products, design compelling upsell offers, integrate them into the CTA area of your product page.

**Detailed Actions:**
1. **Identify Upsell Opportunities:**
    - Analyze the product catalog to identify complementary products or services that can be offered as upsells.
    - Consider customer purchase history and behavior to determine the most relevant upsell items.
2. **Design Upsell Offers:**
    - Create compelling upsell offers that provide additional value to the customer.
    - Ensure the offers are clearly communicated and easy to understand.
3. **Integrate Upsell into Main CTA:**
    - Modify the main Call-To-Action (CTA) on the product page to include the upsell offer.
    - Use persuasive language and visual cues to highlight the upsell without distracting from the primary CTA.
checkpoint.justificationsBenefits: By implementing this checkpoint, you can significantly increase your average order value and drive revenue growth while enhancing overall shopping experience.
